I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. With the same rules, the script reproduces all 10 of your Q2 reference values exactly, so I'm confident the definitions are applied correctly.

| Question | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment by net sales | `smb`, 316,534,383 won |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 248 |
| c. Top category by net sales | `svc`, 312,755,660 won |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | `2025-07` |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | `u93@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 240 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 692,548 won |
| h. September vs. August growth | -3.3% |

The data needed three adjustments before the Q2 values matched:

1. **Time zone:** order times are stored in UTC, but the quarter boundaries and months only match Q2 when converted to Korean time (UTC+9). So an order at 2025-06-30 16:00 UTC counts as July 1 and falls in Q3.
2. **Segment labels:** the same segment is written in different ways (e.g. `SMB`, `smb`, `Enterprise ` with a trailing space). I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.
3. **Duplicate emails:** some emails belong to more than one customer ID. Q2's customer counts for b and f only match when customers are counted by email, so I counted them that way.

The DB has no April orders at all, so in Q2 the comparison for h (May vs. June) worked on that data. Q3 has orders in all three months.
